battle.name: 朱通吉部落入侵雷蒂亞
battle.brief: 259年，日耳曼小部族朱通吉人聯同阿勒曼尼諸部越過多瑙河，掠奪萊蒂亞行省。260年4月24至25日，萊蒂亞總督革尼阿利斯在奧格斯堡擊敗退卻中的聯軍並立凱旋碑，波斯圖莫斯隨即在軍中被推舉為皇帝。卡面的亞述長矛是古代方陣刺擊矛，與日耳曼長矛、羅馬標槍同屬「盾後刺擊」血統，本役並無此器。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 這場衝突是公元259至260年羅馬帝國與多瑙河以北日耳曼部族聯盟之間的一場邊境戰爭，戰場在萊蒂亞行省與其外側的上多瑙河地帶。羅馬一方是瓦勒里安王朝末期、伽利埃努斯在位時的帝國中央軍：萊蒂亞總督馬庫斯·辛普利基尼烏斯·革尼阿利斯直接指揮當地駐防部隊與從高盧、濱海省抽調的預備隊，第八奧古斯塔軍團等主力大隊沿多瑙河上游據點布防，輔以騎兵大隊與輔兵砲兵大隊；皇帝伽利埃努斯本人被東方戰線拖住，根本無暇西顧。羅馬的控制體系在259年出現斷裂：皇帝瓦勒里安在波斯戰役中被沙普爾的波斯王公俘虜，其子卡爾斯·諾圖斯在科隆一線的戰鬥後身亡，使帝國西半部的指揮鏈在數月之內連失兩環。日耳曼一方是朱通吉人為主幹的聯軍。朱通吉人很可能是塞姆農人的一支，屬廣義阿勒曼尼集團，駐地大致在今日巴伐利亞北部、多瑙河以北的上萊茵與上易北之間；他們與阿勒曼尼、庫阿迪、布爾根齊奧內斯諸部共用同一條越境與掠奪路線。原始史料對名稱並不一致：德克西波斯稱其為「朱通吉人」，《奧古斯都史》稱「馬科曼尼人」，佐西莫斯稱「阿勒曼尼」，而羅馬人自己在260年4月所立的奧格斯堡凱旋碑上明確寫成「塞姆農人、或更確切地說朱通吉人的蠻族部落」，這種分歧說明這支部落在羅馬人眼中是一個尚未分離清楚的混合集團，而不是單一王國。聯軍沒有固定的中央指揮，行動以部落聯盟式的分散劫掠為主，作戰時由各部族酋長臨時協同。
countriesEn: This conflict was a frontier war fought between the Roman Empire and a coalition of Germanic tribes from beyond the Danube in AD 259–260, on the soil of the province of Raetia and the upper Danube region outside it. The Roman side was the field army of the late Valerian dynasty under emperor Gallienus: the provincial governor of Raetia, Marcus Simplicinius Genialis, commanded the local garrison together with reserve detachments drawn from Gaul and the coastal provinces, with legions such as Legio VIII Augusta manning the forts along the upper Danube and supported by cavalry and auxiliary artillery units. The emperor Gallienus himself was pinned down in the east and could not help. The Roman command structure broke down in 259: the emperor Valerian was taken prisoner by Shapur's Persian nobles in the eastern campaign, and his son Carinus died in the fighting near Cologne later that year, so that within a few months the chain of command in the western half of the empire lost two of its top links. On the Germanic side stood a coalition whose backbone was the Juthungi (Iuthungi). The Juthungi were probably a branch of the Semnones, belonging to the wider Alamannic grouping, and were settled roughly north of the Danube in what is now northern Bavaria, between the upper Rhine and the upper Elbe; they shared the same routes of crossing and plunder with the Alemanni, the Quadi and the Burgundiones. The ancient sources disagree about their name: Dexippus calls them Juthungi, the Historia Augusta calls them Marcomanni, Zosimus calls them Alemanni, while the Romans themselves, on the Augsburg victory altar raised in AD 260, wrote 'the barbarian people of the Semnones, or, more precisely, of the Juthungi'. That divergence shows that the Romans were dealing with a mixed group not yet clearly separated in their own eyes rather than with a single kingdom. The coalition had no central command of its own; action was carried on as a dispersed series of tribal raids, the chiefs of the different groups coordinating only on the spot.
people: 關鍵人物集中在羅馬一側，日耳曼方面留下的名字極少。朱通吉人沒有留下可考的統帥姓名，260年敗績之後唯一有名字的角色是271年派往奧勒利安宮廷的使者。據德克西波斯記載，這名使者不但沒有求饒，反而宣稱朱通吉人「只拿出很小一部分兵力就攻打多瑙河沿岸的城市，幾乎佔領整個意大利」，並自報「四萬騎兵，而且不是混編的雜兵、不是軟弱的兵，全是朱通吉人，我們以騎兵作戰的聲名素著」；步兵則是騎兵的兩倍。使者要求維持羅馬向各部族提供的例行「饋贈」，被奧勒利安以威脅回絕，聯軍才倉皇退去。羅馬方面的關鍵人物有三人。其一是萊蒂亞總督馬庫斯·辛普利基尼烏斯·革尼阿利斯，正是他在260年4月24日至25日追擊並擊退越過多瑙河的朱通吉聯軍，並在事後於奧格斯堡立下凱旋碑，碑文自稱擊敗「塞姆農人、或更確切地說朱通吉人」。其二是波斯圖莫斯，這位第八奧古斯塔軍團的指揮官在萊蒂亞的戰役中率軍破敵，隨後被士兵推舉為皇帝，於260年建立高盧帝國，並在261年內卡河一役再敗阿勒曼尼聯軍。其三是皇帝伽利埃努斯與後來的奧勒利安：前者因東方戰事無法支援萊蒂亞，後者在271年於提契諾與法諾連勝朱通吉聯軍，終結了這條戰線。同期記錄者德克西波斯、佐西莫斯與奧勒里安·維克托爾，是今日能重建這場戰爭的主要文本來源。
peopleEn: Almost all the named actors stand on the Roman side; the Germanic side left behind almost no personal names at all. No Juthungi commander is known by name, and the only identifiable figure is the envoy the Juthungi sent to the court of Aurelian in 271. Dexippus records that this envoy did not sue for mercy but announced that the Juthungi 'with a very small part of our military resources attacked the cities near the Danube and almost took possession of all Italy', adding that 'we campaigned with cavalry numbering forty thousand, and these were not mixed men, nor weak men, but purely Iuthungi, who have a great reputation for fighting on horseback', and that their infantry was twice the size of the cavalry. The envoy demanded the continuation of the customary 'gifts' the Romans paid the tribes; Aurelian refused and threatened them, and only then did the coalition withdraw. Three men dominate the Roman side. The first is Marcus Simplicinius Genialis, governor of Raetia, who caught and broke the Juthungi coalition after it had crossed the Danube on 24 and 25 April AD 260 and raised the Augsburg victory altar, calling the enemy 'the barbarian people of the Semnones, or, more precisely, of the Juthungi'. The second is Postumus, commander of Legio VIII Augusta, who led the field army in Raetia, was acclaimed emperor by his own men, founded the Gallic Empire in 260, and defeated the Alamanni again at the Neckar in 261. The third pair are the emperors Gallienus and Aurelian: the first could not spare forces from the eastern front for Raetia, the second beat the Juthungi coalition at Ticinum and Fanum Fortunae in 271 and closed that front. The contemporaries Dexippus, Zosimus and Aurelius Victor are the principal textual sources by which this war can be reconstructed today.
kits: 卡面兵器是亞述長矛，年代標為公元前900年，屬新亞述王國的步兵裝備：短柄、長刃、鐵鏃，與弓、斧一同配發，供密集方陣中的戰士在盾後刺擊。它並不屬於259年的戰場，但它在這場戰爭裡的位置是把話說到源頭——羅馬的近身刺擊武器與日耳曼人的長矛，都屬於這一條「盾加刺擊矛」的血統，只是在公元3世紀已經換成鐵、換成長度、也換成不同的戰術用法。實際上打這場仗的雙方各有自己的矛。羅馬步兵以短刺槍與輕型標槍配大盾，標槍的鐵矛頭做成長而窄的圓錐形，配一截木柄，擲出後仍可撿回半截再用的設計在守城與野戰都用；貴族少年與騎兵用直刃的短劍，步兵甲是分段的鱗甲與札甲，行軍靠帳篷與驢車。營務與攻城配備有配重式擲石器、角弓弩、攻城塔，以及壕溝工程的斧、鍬、鐮。輔軍還有載重用的牛車與渡河用的皮囊。日耳曼方面最代表性的武器是「弗拉梅亞」式的長矛：柄長約一點八至二點四公尺，鐵矛頭寬而略帶翼形，兼具直刺與擲刺兩用，配大圓盾使用；近身有柳葉形鐵短劍與單刃獵刀，盾有圓形，也有偏長的六角形與龜形盾板。無攻城器，無投石器，全靠人馬突擊與縱火毀糧。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is an Assyrian spear dated to 900 BC, the infantry arm of the Neo-Assyrian kingdom: a short haft, a long blade and an iron head, issued together with bow and axe to men fighting in dense ranks behind shields. It was not present in AD 259, but its place in this war is as a point of origin: the Roman close-quarter thrusting arm and the Germanic spear both descend from that same 'shield and thrusting spear' tradition, though by the third century the metal, the length and the tactical use had all changed. The two sides actually fighting in AD 260 each had their own spears. Roman infantry used the short thrusting spear and the light javelin (pilum) together with the large curved shield (scutum); the iron head of the pilum was a long narrow cone fitted to a short wooden shaft, and its design allowed the broken shaft to be recovered and reused, which mattered both in sieges and in the field. Young aristocrats and cavalry used the straight-bladed short sword (gladius); infantry wore segmented scale and segmentary armour; the baggage train and the engineers brought in the ballista and the onager, with towers, axes, picks and sickles for siege and entrenchment work. Ox wagons and inflated skins for crossing rivers handled transport. On the Germanic side the characteristic weapon was the framea-style long spear: a shaft of roughly 1.8 to 2.4 metres with a broad, slightly flanged iron head usable for both thrusting and throwing, carried with a large round shield; close to the line they had iron long swords with leaf-shaped blades and single-edged seaxes, and their shields were round, elongated hexagonal or tortoise-shaped. They had no siege engines and no artillery: everything rested on the shock of men and horses, on fire and on plunder.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術，是三世紀蠻族戰爭的典型樣式與羅馬邊防反擊體系的結合。日耳曼聯軍的入侵遵循一套固定程序：挑選多瑙河防線守備鬆懈或冬季結冰可通行的段落，分批越境，入境後不以爭奪正面會戰為目標，而是分成數個縱隊平行推進，掃掠城邑、集落、谷地裡的儲糧與牲口，盡量在羅馬騎兵與主力集結前轉移，同時派輕騎偵察羅軍縱隊的位置；寧可避開羅馬密集步兵方陣，也不願在不利地形上與其硬拼。260年的戰役中，朱通吉聯軍正是這樣深入到萊蒂亞腹地並分兵掠奪，才使羅馬邊防軍得以用騎兵搜索、以小隊步兵在預設陣地上截擊。羅馬方面的反擊戰術有幾個可考特點。第一是「追擊殲滅」而非正面殲滅：革尼阿利斯在奧格斯堡之戰中不是正面攻擊敵陣，而是在退卻中的聯軍側後追上，迫使對方丟下戰利品與輜重潰散；凱旋碑上堆積的戰利品、繳獲的武器與被押著的俘虜，記錄的正是這種追擊後的清理場面，而非激烈對攻。第二是密集步兵核心加騎兵兩翼的標準編組：羅軍靠重裝步兵方陣頂住壓力，靠騎兵迂迴切斷退路。第三是地形控制：261年內卡河之役，羅軍在萊蒂亞邊境要塞萊瑙附近迎敵，把戰場壓在河谷與河曲之間，使敵軍一旦戰敗就難以散開，並在渡口佈防切斷北岸退路。第四是把勝利「固化」成石頭：260年的奧格斯堡凱旋碑與261年的萊瑙凱旋碑都是戰後就地樹立，把戰利品、俘虜與銘文公開展示，等於向全帝國宣告邊防已經恢復。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this war combine the standard pattern of third-century barbarian campaigning with the Roman frontier counter-stroke system. The Germanic coalition followed a fixed procedure: it chose a stretch of the Danube line where the garrison was thin or where the winter ice could be crossed, moved over in several parties, and once inside the empire refused to seek a set-piece battle, instead splitting into parallel columns that swept through towns, villages and the granaries and cattle of the valleys, shifting position before Roman cavalry and field armies could concentrate, and sending light horsemen ahead to scout the Roman columns. They would rather avoid a pitched clash with a dense Roman infantry block than fight a set-piece action on unfavourable ground. That is exactly how the Juthungi coalition in AD 260 pushed deep into Raetia and fanned out into plundering, which allowed the Roman frontier troops to hunt them down with cavalry and to intercept them in small detachments of infantry on ground chosen in advance. The Roman counter-stroke shows several identifiable features. First, it was a pursuit and mopping-up operation rather than a battle of annihilation: at the battle near Augsburg, Genialis did not assault the enemy position frontally but caught the coalition while it was withdrawing, forcing it to abandon booty and wagons and to scatter; the trophies, captured weapons and bound prisoner carved on the altar record the clearing-up that followed a pursuit, not a frontal slugfest. Second, the Roman order of battle was the standard one: a mass of armoured infantry in the centre to absorb the shock, with cavalry working round the flank to cut off the retreat. Third, terrain control: at the Neckar in 261 the Roman army fought near the frontier fort at Rainau, pressed the enemy into the river bend and the valley so that defeat meant dispersal, and covered the crossings to shut the northern bank route. Fourth, victory was petrified in stone: the Augsburg altar of 260 and the Rainau monument of 261 were raised on the spot after the fighting, publicly displaying booty, prisoners and an inscription, and announcing to the whole empire that the frontier had been restored.
data: 可核對的數字不多，但有幾個硬點。其一是最關鍵的日期：奧格斯堡凱旋碑的銘文以「pridie Kalendas Maias」（四月二十四日）記錄擊退敵軍之日，以「Kalendas Maias」（四月二十五日）記錄立碑之日，即公元260年4月24至25日。碑體在1992年於奧格斯堡出土，今屬該市羅馬博物館，是本戰役唯一的同時代實物紀錄。其二是年代框架：入侵本身被記在259至260年，波斯圖莫斯被推舉為皇帝是在260年，內卡河之役在261年，第二次入侵意大利在270至271年，奧勒利安在提契諾與法諾的勝利在271年。其三是尺寸與距離的量級：日耳曼長矛弗拉梅亞長約一點八至二點四公尺，羅馬標槍約兩公尺，羅馬短劍刃長約五十至六十公分；萊蒂亞行省的多瑙河防線自雷根斯堡至帕紹一線約一百三十公里；奧格斯堡距多瑙河最近處不足兩百公里，正是「越境—深入—被追回」之間的距離尺度。其四是敵方自述的兵力：朱通吉使者在271年宣稱的騎兵四萬、步兵為騎兵兩倍，是德克西波斯記下的敵方說法，學界多視為誇大以示聲勢，不宜當作成交的實數。這場戰役的羅馬損耗與敵方損失，史料都沒有留下可用數字，本卡不填推測值。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are few, but a few are solid. The first is the crucial date: the inscription of the Augsburg victory altar records the day the enemy was beaten back as the 'pridie Kalendas Maias' (24 April) and the day the altar was dedicated as the 'Kalendas Maias' (25 April), that is 24 to 25 April AD 260. The altar was excavated at Augsburg in 1992 and belongs to the city's Roman museum; it is the only contemporary artefact of this war. Second is the chronological frame: the incursion is placed in AD 259–260; Postumus was acclaimed emperor in 260; the battle at the Neckar belongs to 261; the second invasion of Italy to 270–271; Aurelian's victories at Ticinum and Fanum Fortunae to 271. Third, dimensions and distances: the Germanic framea ran about 1.8 to 2.4 metres, the Roman pilum about two metres, the Roman short sword blade some fifty to sixty centimetres; the Danube frontier of Raetia ran roughly a hundred and thirty kilometres from Castra Regina to Boiodurum; and Augsburg lies less than two hundred kilometres from the nearest point of the Danube, which is the scale of 'crossing, penetration, being driven back' that the campaign describes. Fourth, the enemy's own claimed strength: the forty thousand horsemen and twice as many foot announced by the Juthungi envoy in 271 is what Dexippus recorded, and it is generally read as a boast meant to impress, not as an establishment figure. Neither Roman nor Germanic losses are recorded in usable numbers, and this card fills in no invented value.
cause: 打起嚟的原因是多層的，最表層是帝國西部的空虛。259年瓦勒里安在波斯被俘，次年其子卡爾斯·諾圖斯在萊蒂亞方向對波斯圖莫斯的戰鬥中陣亡，皇帝伽利埃努斯本人又被東方戰事拖住，萊蒂亞與上多瑙河之間那段邊防的指揮鏈連續失去最高層，邊軍只能按各鎮的判斷自行應戰，而朱通吉聯軍正是看準這段空檔才越境。中層原因是羅馬邊防體系本身的結構性弱點。萊蒂亞的多瑙河防線沿線多為小鎮與要塞，駐軍編制有限，一旦敵人越過一段邊界並且向縱深分散，縱使邊軍立刻出擊，也只能逐股追擊，很難一次合圍。整個三世紀，日耳曼部族已把「越境劫掠、退回多瑙河北」做成慣例，甚至形成了向羅馬索取例行饋贈的默契：羅馬用金子買和平，雙方都清楚這是交易而非臣屬。深層原因是三世紀危機對帝國信譽的打擊。戰俘皇帝與接連的敗績讓帝國在邊境內部的威信下降，各地守軍的士氣與裝備補給都受影響，鄰近行省的貴族與地方勢力也各自求自保，削弱了中央可以調動的力量。而日耳曼世界這邊，同族不同部族的聯盟在成功越境後會分享掠奪物，進一步刺激其他部落加入，使一次邊境突破變成跨多瑙河的集體行動。
causeEn: The reasons are layered, and the surface one is the emptiness of the western empire. In 259 Valerian was taken prisoner in the east, in 260 his son Carinus died in the fighting against Postumus in the Raetian sector, and Gallienus himself was tied down on the eastern front; the command chain of the Raetia and upper Danube sector lost its highest links in a row, and the frontier troops could only act on the judgement of each fortress command, while the Juthungi coalition chose that moment precisely because of the gap. The middle layer is the structural weakness of the Roman frontier system. The Danube line in Raetia consisted of small towns and forts with limited garrisons; once an enemy had crossed one stretch and dispersed inland, the frontier troops could only chase it in separate columns and rarely close a ring. Throughout the third century the Germanic tribes had turned 'cross, plunder, fall back beyond the Danube' into a routine, and in places even into a bargain, the Romans paying gold for peace while both sides understood the arrangement as a transaction rather than submission. The deepest layer is the damage the third-century crisis did to imperial prestige. A captured emperor and a run of defeats lowered the empire's authority at the frontier; the morale and resupply of the frontier garrisons suffered with it, and the provincial elites and local powers in the frontier zones, absorbed in their own self-defence, weakened the strength the centre could call up. On the Germanic side, tribes of one and the same stock shared the plunder of a successful crossing, which pulled further groups in and turned a single frontier breach into a collective movement across the Danube.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接後果，是羅馬帝國西部出現了一個獨立政權。260年波斯圖莫斯在萊蒂亞被推舉為皇帝，率軍渡萊茵河進入高盧，之後逐步控制高盧、不列顛與西班牙的西班牙行省，建立高盧帝國並延續到269年。它由一次邊境戰敗直接催生，說明259至260年的連串蠻族入侵已經嚴重到帝國西部必須自立的地步。與此同時，高盧帝國的存在也讓萊蒂亞的戰線得以維持：波斯圖莫斯及後繼者把防禦重心放在萊茵河與多瑙河上游，萊蒂亞防線反而得到喘息與整補。更長期的影響有幾層。第一，羅馬把帝國東部的優先應付策略被徹底否定，260年代後期開始，帝國把大量兵力與資源從東方調回多瑙河與萊茵河，前線由巡邏式防禦改為設防式防禦，沿線增建要塞、塔樓與壕溝，並用收編的蠻族兵充當輔軍與屯田兵。第二，261年以來的戰役讓日耳曼部族學到羅馬邊防的虛實，阿勒曼尼聯軍的越境規模在接下來數十年不減反增，阿勒曼尼戰爭一路延續到四世紀，成為羅馬晚期最長期的邊境消耗戰之一。第三，就軍事宣傳而言，260年奧格斯堡凱旋碑與261年萊瑙凱旋碑這類戰勝紀念碑，在普遍缺乏皇帝的第三世紀成為帝國合法性的重要物證，它們把邊軍的一次勝利放大成帝國的秩序象徵。第四，271年朱通吉聯軍再侵意大利、奧勒利安在提契諾與法諾獲勝，則為隨後272至273年收復高盧、不列顛與西班牙、終結高盧帝國鋪了路；再加上291年戴克里先的全盤改革與四世紀邊防體系的定型，這一連串戰爭最終把羅馬的帝國結構重新拉回有效狀態。
impactEn: The direct consequence of the war was the appearance of an independent state in the west of the empire. In 260 Postumus was acclaimed emperor in Raetia, crossed the Rhine into Gaul and by degrees took control of Gaul, Britain and the Spanish provinces of Hispania, founding the Gallic Empire that lasted until 269. It was born directly out of a frontier defeat, which shows that the run of barbarian incursions of 259–260 had gone far enough for the western half of the empire to stand on its own. At the same time, the existence of the Gallic Empire let the Raetian front breathe: Postumus and his successors put the main weight of their defence on the Rhine and the upper Danube, and the Raetian line was given time to recover and to be refitted. The longer-term effects run in several directions. First, the strategy of prioritising the eastern theatre was refuted outright; from the late 260s the empire shifted troops and resources back to the Danube and the Rhine, changed the frontier from a patrolling defence to a fortified one, built more forts, towers and ditches along the line, and used recruited barbarian troops as auxiliaries and as settlers on the farms. Second, the campaigns from 261 onwards taught the Germanic tribes the layout of the Roman frontier, and the scale of the Alamannic incursions grew rather than shrank in the following decades: the Alamannic wars ran on into the fourth century and became one of the longest drains on the late empire's resources. Third, in military terms, the victory monuments of 260 at Augsburg and 261 at Rainau became important evidence of legitimacy in a third century short of emperors; they magnified one frontier victory into a symbol of imperial order. Fourth, the renewed invasion of Italy by the Juthungi coalition in 271 and Aurelian's victories at Ticinum and Fanum Fortunae cleared the way for the recovery of Gaul, Britain and Spain in 272–273 and the end of the Gallic Empire; added to the wholesale reform of Diocletian in 291 and the fixing of the frontier system in the fourth century, this sequence of wars eventually pulled the imperial structure back into working order.
result: 結局分三段看。第一段是260年4月24至25日的奧格斯堡之戰：朱通吉聯軍在掠奪萊蒂亞縱深之後，於退卻或轉進途中被萊蒂亞總督革尼阿利斯率軍追上並擊破，奧格斯堡凱旋碑記載的就是這次「蠻族部落塞姆農人、或更確切地說朱通吉人」的失敗；聯軍被逐回多瑙河北，掠奪所得大量淪為羅軍戰利品，凱旋碑上的繳獲武器與俘虜即是證物。羅軍本身代價有限，史料未留下損失數字。第二段是260至261年的政治與軍事連續反應：軍隊在萊蒂亞推舉波斯圖莫斯為皇帝，隨後在261年的內卡河之役中再敗阿勒曼尼聯軍，萊瑙凱旋碑為此而立，戰線重回上萊茵與多瑙河的均勢；此後朱通吉人沒有立刻再犯。第三段是270至271年的第二次入侵：聯軍再度越過多瑙河進入意大利，初期在皮亞琴察附近失利，但奧勒利安很快在法諾與提契諾連勝，擊潰其主力，迫使殘部退回多瑙河以北，渡河時溺死者無數。朱通吉使者隨後到羅馬求和並要求恢復例行饋贈，奧勒利安拒絕並發出威脅，聯軍才帶著殘兵離去。戰線至此回到萊蒂亞與上多瑙河一帶；雖然第三世紀此後仍有零星越境，但259年這場以凱旋碑為記錄的入侵，成為了羅馬西部邊防長期重建的起點。
resultEn: The outcome reads in three stages. The first is the battle near Augsburg of 24 to 25 April AD 260: after plundering the depth of Raetia, the Juthungi coalition was caught while withdrawing or shifting position and broken by the troops of the Raetian governor Genialis; the Augsburg victory altar records the defeat of 'the barbarian people of the Semnones, or, more precisely, of the Juthungi'. The coalition was driven back beyond the Danube and much of the plunder fell into Roman hands as booty, the captured weapons and the prisoner on the altar being the evidence. Roman losses were limited and no figures survive. The second stage is the political and military reaction of 260 to 261: the army in Raetia acclaimed Postumus emperor, and in 261 the Romans broke the Alamanni coalition again at the Neckar, the Rainau monument being raised for that victory, so that the front returned to something like parity along the upper Rhine and Danube. The Juthungi did not immediately raid again. The third stage is the second invasion of 270 to 271: the coalition crossed the Danube into Italy again, was checked and defeated at first near Placentia, but Aurelian won in quick succession at Fanum Fortunae and Ticinum, broke its main body and forced the remnants back beyond the Danube, with many drowning in the crossing. The Juthungi envoys then came to Rome to seek peace and to demand the resumption of the customary payments; Aurelian refused, threatened them, and only then did they depart with what was left of their army. The front thus settled again around Raetia and the upper Danube; although scattered crossings continued through the rest of the third century, the invasion recorded on the Augsburg altar became the starting point of the long rebuild of the western frontier.
